title: I Used the Fermenter Carboy Shelf on the Club Member Who Took My Airlock

parts.text: I checked shelf C at 7:07 p.m. and member Nix was already swapping my numbered airlock. The card said: ONE SHELF. FOURTEEN DAYS. AIRLOCK STAYS WITH THE CARBOY. I was thirty, club member, holding a gravity sheet that listed our batch. Nix shrugged. "Members are the shelf." I photographed the card, the log, and his bung on my carboy. Then I asked for the shelf sheet. At 7:15 the cellar pinged why Nix's name was on my lock. I kept my voice cellar-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A card is only a card until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The cellar can see Nix's bung on my carboy during our fourteen.

social.video_title: He swapped my numbered airlock on my carboy — Part 1/2
social.description: Fermenter shelf, a member on my bung, a fourteen-day card he posted. I logged the swap. Would you have asked for the shelf sheet?

parts.text: Nix called it a burp until the cellar asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the card, and the bung still. The airlock went back to my carboy. Nix ran his own fourteen and told the next member atmosphere was always about krausen. Krausen is a word members use when a card exists. Shelf policy now has a second line: MEMBERS ARE NOT THE SHELF. I keep our lock on a labeled hook. Nix brown-bags his jokes. The cellar finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Members are not the shelf — Part 2/2
social.description: Shelf sheet, numbered airlock, and a second line on the card. Was a burp ever my bung?
